---
title: "How do I find the proportion where A or B happens, avoiding double-counting?"
---

## Question

How do I find the proportion where A or B happens, avoiding double-counting?

## Work through it

Define both events on aligned rows; exclude incomplete pairs; calculate P(A), P(B), and P(A AND B); subtract the overlap or count logical OR.

## Worked example: airquality

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("airquality")
result <- ru_apply("probability_union", data=d,
                   x=d$Ozone>60, y=d$Temp>=80, event=TRUE, given=TRUE)
stopifnot(result["either"]>=result["A"],result["either"]<=1)
```

The either-event fraction includes ozone readings above 60, temperatures at least 80°F, or both. Subtracting the overlap prevents counting the same day twice.

## Adapt to another question

```r
ru_apply("probability_union", data=your_data, x=your_data$A, y=your_data$B, event=TRUE, given=TRUE)
```

'Either but not both' is exclusive OR, a different question requiring a different calculation.

Check the input conditions with `ru_plan("probability_union")` before treating a calculation as an inference.
